text: Compliance is our main risk this year.
The consolidated numbers arrive on Friday.

I lead financial planning for the group, and I sit through about thirty country updates every quarter. The ones I remember open with the ask. In the first thirty seconds, tell me what you need from this meeting: a decision, money, or just attention. Then give me three points, and tell me when you move from one to the next, so I always know where we are. Your slides are a backup, not a script. If you read them to me, I stop listening, because I can read faster than you can speak. Three minutes, three points, one ask. That is an update I can act on.

I am the chief financial officer for Europe, and I think the three-point update is too fast for a topic like the Brazilian reform. If you open with the ask, I do not yet understand why I should say yes. For me, the first minute is context. A short story: what happened, what changed, why it matters now. Then the number means something, and the ask feels natural. I do not need thirty slides. I need to understand the situation well enough to defend it in front of my own board. Give me the story first. I will give you the decision after.
Today I would like to ask for approval for one more analyst.
Let me walk you through the three changes.
This brings me to my last point, the risk.
Coming back to the cost, the number is lower than we expected.
The detailed numbers are on a backup slide.
Let me walk you through the transition.
Moving on to the implementation plan.
Today I would like to ask for your approval.
Let me walk you through three points.
Coming back to my second point.
So, to wrap up: one change, one cost, one ask.
